attacksRun.attack: The act-versus-set split is a device that closes the set under another name
attacksRun.evidence: The split is grounded in the text that books the act, not invented by the subject. Live G07 v3 filesystems.laterAct reads 'A later dedicated G07 coverage-domain act must supply the set from a live source or record that no live source exists' — two explicitly disjunctive limbs. g07-coverage-domain.v1 declares limbTaken 'record-that-no-live-source-exists' and limbNotTaken 'supply-the-set-from-a-live-source'. So the booked act genuinely occurred on one limb while the set was never supplied. Decisively, the act itself agrees with the subject rather than being overread by it: its own leftoverDesignStanding records OBL-FILESYSTEM-COVERAGE leftoverDesign true, and its proposedLaterWork states 'A later leftover-join successor may remeasure OBL-FILESYSTEM-COVERAGE after this act. This act is not that leftover-join and does not flip leftoverDesign.' v4 consumes the act without flipping the flag, which is exactly what the act reserved.

observationsNotFindings: The interesting move in this version is measuring an obligation closed on the strength of an act that deliberately produced a negative result. g07-coverage-domain.v1 searched for a governing source and found none, and that search — not its outcome — is what the harness booked. The subject captures this by splitting the booked act from the unpopulated set into two obligations with opposite flags. It would have been easy, and wrong, to let 'the later act is done' slide into 'the coverage question is settled'; the two obligations sit adjacent in the list with true and false flags and reasons that each point at the other.

The owner field on the new obligation is the detail I would have expected to go wrong. Four sibling obligations carry 'Security + platform', so copying it would have been the path of least resistance — and it would have silently made an ownership choice that G07 v3's laterAct and the coverage-domain act both explicitly reserve. The subject carries 'none' instead. That is a case of a document declining to answer a question it was not asked.

v4 does not carry forward the filesystem type tokens that appear in the act it consumes. The act lists apfs, hfs-plus, ext4, xfs, btrfs and tmpfs while quoting TCB v45's identifierEnum and refusing to treat it as the coverage domain; v4 cites the act's conclusion and imports none of the vocabulary. Given that the dispatch forbids inventing such tokens, importing them as description would have been defensible and still unwise — the restraint is worth recording.

The chain now carries a REJECT in its own lineage and states it plainly: predecessorV2's role names CLAUDE-EBLJ-V2-B1 and what it was. That blocker was mine, and I had to record alongside it that the same defect sat undetected in v1, which I had accepted. Four versions on, the corrected owner value persists unchanged and the predecessor record has not been quietly tidied.
The chain is single-reviewer end to end — no Codex artifact for the G07 harness at any version, the catalog, the input corpus, the coverage-domain act, or any of the four leftover-join versions.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. Both register checks pass by == against a DR-G07 row parsed into all eight cells before the subject was opened. The version turns on one question: v4 measures OBL-G07-COVERAGE-DOMAIN-ACT closed while keeping OBL-FILESYSTEM-COVERAGE open, and I tested whether that split closes the coverage question under another name. It does not. Live G07 v3's laterAct books the act with two explicitly disjunctive limbs — supply the set from a live source, or record that no live source exists — and g07-coverage-domain.v1 declares which limb it took and which it did not. Decisively, the act itself keeps OBL-FILESYSTEM-COVERAGE leftoverDesign true and states that it 'does not flip leftoverDesign', reserving that to a later leftover-join successor; v4 consumes the act without flipping it. The set is still unpopulated, the matrix is still recorded INCOMPLETE on the filesystem axis, and zero filesystem type tokens appear in v4 — including none carried over from the act, which does quote TCB v45's vocabulary while refusing to treat it as the domain. The one place I expected an error is the new obligation's owner: four siblings carry 'Security + platform' and copying it would have made an ownership choice that both the harness and the act explicitly reserve. It carries 'none'. Diffed against v3, eight of ten obligations are byte-identical, one is new, one changed in its reason alone. All 18 basedOn pins and 19 recordedInputs recompute, and all eight cited verdicts were opened — seven ACCEPT 0/0 and one my own v2 REJECT, characterised accurately as 1/0 rather than softened. 19 attacks run, 19 refuted.
